title: fix(service-record-context): a related object the stack does not define states nothing
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DLCo5F2y7fgbM8tstGoyyUn)_

Fixes #37486
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读
- 用户能看到什么变化：资料包里关联了一个系统中根本不存在的对象（作者写错名字）时，AI 工具不再对任何人说「部分资料对你不可见」，只是不给这一节；真有权限限制的对象照旧提示。
- 为什么做：属于「记录范围的 AI 问询」这一组后续，让工具行为与设计一致：作者写错由校验报给作者，不伪装成权限问题。
- 出错会怎样：最坏是某个确实存在、只是此人看不到的对象漏了「不可见」提示；两种情况都有真实内核测试守着，可直接撤回此改动。
- 要你做的：无。设计文档需补一句（见下方英文节），随另一张设计文档修订卡一并提交。

## What changes

`executeGetRecordContext` step 4a (`packages/services/service-record-context/src/record-context-tools.ts`): a `related` child that passes the read guard and API exposure and that this caller is not served is still left out and never read again. The `not_visible` statement now fires only when the door's **published** definition of the object exists (`door.publishedObjectDefinitionOf`). A name the published definitions lack is an author defect (ADR-0160 D1, `os validate` reports it as `ai-context-object-unknown`) and states nothing (D3: "A name the published definition lacks is an author defect ([D1](#d1)) and fires nothing.").

Why this fact: it is the same for every caller. Both door implementations were read on `origin/main` 579b8577:
- HTTP (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`, `publishedObjectDefinitionOf` → `readServedObject`): the protocol's merged `getMetaItems({ type: 'object' })` listing, with no caller argument, or the metadata service's `getObject`. No masker. An absent name answers `undefined` → `null`, no throw.
- stdio (`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`, `readObjectDeclaration`): `getMetaItemForExecution` / `getMetaItem` by name, falling back to the metadata service's copy; no principal. An absent name answers `undefined` → `null`. Its one rethrow is `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, which API exposure has already refused one step earlier.
- `assertApiExposed` on the HTTP door is `refuseUnexposedDataAction(..., 'refuse')`: on no declaration it falls open to schema defaults (`apiEnabled` true), so an undefined object reaches step 4a's served read on both doors, as the card said.

A throw from the new read is judged the way every other step-4a read is: a coded refusal refuses the call unnamed, any other throw fails it `INTERNAL_ERROR` 500 naming nothing (`refusedOrFailed`). The definition is used as a boolean only; nothing of it is carried.

Comments in the same file that said a left-out child's definition is never read are corrected to say what the code now does.

## ADR-0160 amendment owed

D3 "Object level", the bullet "A `related` child that this caller is not served is left out.", says "Nothing of the child is read, its definition included." This change reads the child's **published** definition once, for whether the stack defines it at all. Proposed replacement for that sentence (to ride #37386's ADR-0160 edit; `docs/adr/**` is not touched here):

> Nothing of the child is read except its published definition, which is asked once, for whether the stack defines the object at all: a name the published definitions lack is an author defect ([D1](#d1)), left out with no statement for every caller. The published definition is the same for every caller, so whether the statement fires depends on this caller's served schema alone, and nothing of the definition is carried.

## Tests

<details><summary>Measured first: the real-kernel case red on main (both doors agree, both carry the note)</summary>

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/mcp-record-context-tools-bridge.test.ts` at 7adbe2d2 (tests only, `src/` = main 579b8577):

```
× [ADR-0160 D1/D3] a related entry naming an object the stack does not define leaves its section out and states nothing: the same bytes for both callers, on both doors
AssertionError: expected [ { kind: 'not_visible', …(1) } ] to deeply equal []
+     "kind": "not_visible",
+     "text": "Some of the material this pack covers is not visible to you, so it is not given. Do not treat it as empty or absent, and do not guess it.",
 Tests  1 failed | 29 passed (30)
```

The `/mcp`-vs-stdio byte equality held before the note assertion, so the defect was on both doors. The two-caller defined-but-unserved case passed on main, as it should.
</details>

<details><summary>Green after the fix, and the ablation</summary>

- `@objectstack/runtime` `src/mcp-record-context-tools-bridge.test.ts`: Tests 30 passed (30).
- `@objectstack/service-record-context` `pnpm test`: Test Files 3 passed (3), Tests 180 passed (180).
- Ablation (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, fix committed first): `if (published) hidden = true;` → `hidden = Boolean('ABLATION_37486');`; `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in 2 built files; the runtime case and the new unit case each went red (1 failed | 29 passed; 1 failed | 132 passed); restore leg: marker absent from all 6 built files, working tree clean against HEAD. A first attempt used a comment marker, which the build strips: its dist reading failed, so that attempt counts for nothing.
</details>

New cases:
- Real kernel, both doors, `packages/runtime/src/mcp-record-context-tools-bridge.test.ts` (shared harness extended with object `rc_partner`, served to `usr_member` through `rc_unmasker` and not to `usr_plain`, and packs `rc_misspelt_child` / `rc_role_child`):
  - an undefined `related` object (`rc_ghost`): no section, `notes` `[]`, the name nowhere, for `usr_member` and `usr_plain`, and the two callers' answers byte-identical;
  - a defined child served to one caller and not the other: its section for `usr_member` with no note; for `usr_plain` no section, one `not_visible` note, `rc_partner` named nowhere.
- Unit, `src/__tests__/record-context-tools.test.ts`: the undefined child states nothing while a hidden field or an unserved defined child beside it still states; a left-out child's published read that throws refuses unnamed (coded) or fails `INTERNAL_ERROR` (uncoded). Two pins that said a left-out child's published definition is never asked now pin the new order: guard, exposure, served read, published read, then nothing.

## Acceptance notes

- The card's Acceptance asks to state the `Clause-②` line because the tool's answer changes; the claim binds `Clause-②: no`, which is what this PR and its changeset carry. Flagged in the report, not re-ruled here.
- The card cites ADR-0160 point 20 (fields); the governing text for an unknown object is D1 and D3.

## Verification

Read first (by risk):
1. `packages/services/service-record-context/src/record-context-tools.ts`, the `if (!served)` hunk of step 4a.
2. `packages/runtime/src/mcp-record-context-tools-bridge.test.ts`, the two new cases and the fixture's `rc_partner` permissions.
3. `packages/services/service-record-context/src/__tests__/record-context-tools.test.ts`, the two re-pinned order assertions.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/mcp-record-context-tools-bridge.test.ts` after building the closure: expect 30 passed, including "a related entry naming an object the stack does not define …".
